prompt.context: Our client is a transportation company, operating buses daily from New York City to Boston. They operate with buses leaving every hour from 7AM to 10PM, inclusive (buses leave at 7AM and 10PM and all hours in between), from both locations.
prompt.question: There are 3 questions you should answer for this case: 1) What is the minimum number of buses the company needs to operate? 2) What are some ways the company can increase profits? 3) How would you value the company?

clarifying_info.q: How long does the trip take between New York and Boston?
What about the time it takes to unload, load passengers, and refuel before making the return trip?
clarifying_info.a: Assume that is negligible — the bus can leave right away to make the return.

clarifying_info.q: Is the company currently operating at capacity?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, assume all buses are 100% filled.

clarifying_info.q: What is the competition like? Can we raise prices?
clarifying_info.a: The market is highly competitive and raising prices would be unwise.

clarifying_info.q: How many seats does each bus have?
clarifying_info.a: 40 seats per bus, operating at capacity.

clarifying_info.q: What does a one-way ticket cost?

exhibits.title: Bus Schedule Diagram
exhibits.shows: A diagram showing bus departure and arrival times for both the New York and Boston locations across all hours from 7:00 AM through 2:00 AM the following day.
exhibits.data: New York departure times: 7:00 AM, 8:00 AM, 9:00 AM, 10:00 AM, 11:00 AM, 12:00 PM, 1:00 PM, 2:00 PM, 3:00 PM, 4:00 PM, 5:00 PM, 6:00 PM, 7:00 PM, 8:00 PM, 9:00 PM, 10:00 PM, 11:00 PM, 12:00 AM, 1:00 AM, 2:00 AM; Boston departure times mirror New York.

framework: Minimum buses needed: map out bus schedules given 4-hour one-way trip and hourly departures 7AM–10PM from both cities; determine how many buses are in service simultaneously

Profit increase: structure as revenue levers vs. cost levers; consider ancillary revenue, schedule expansion, M&A on revenue side; fleet upgrades, operational synergies, labor/marketing cost review on cost side
Company valuation: walk through P&L from revenue to EBITDA; then bridge to FCF via D&A, taxes, capex, and net working capital changes; apply DCF or comparable transaction multiples

questions.prompt: Question 1: What is the minimum number of buses the company needs to operate?
questions.guidance: A bus leaves NY (or BOS) at 7AM, arrives at the other city at 11AM, and can immediately return. The return trip arrives back at 3PM, allowing another departure at 3PM. A single bus therefore covers the 7AM, 11AM, 3PM, 7PM slots from the originating city. Each starting city needs 4 buses covering the 7AM, 8AM, 9AM, 10AM departure slots respectively; the 11AM–10PM hourly slots are covered by these same 4 buses on their cycling return trips. With 4 buses needed from NY and 4 from BOS (because both cities start sending buses at 7AM simultaneously), the total minimum fleet is 8 buses.

math.setup: Trip duration = 4 hours. Buses depart every hour 7AM–10PM = 16 departures per direction. A bus that departs at hour H arrives at hour H+4 and departs back at H+4, returning at H+8.
steps: Buses from NY starting at 7, 8, 9, 10AM are the 'new' buses needed — 4 buses from NY side
Each of these 4 buses cycles: 7AM NY→arrives BOS 11AM→departs BOS 11AM→arrives NY 3PM→departs NY 3PM... covering all subsequent hourly slots
Buses from BOS also start at 7AM simultaneously, requiring 4 additional buses from BOS side

questions.prompt: Question 2: What are some ways the company can increase profits?
questions.guidance: Structure the answer along revenue and cost dimensions. Revenue side: add ancillary services (snacks, magazines on buses or in terminal); add more departures to schedule (though buses arriving after 2AM may have limited demand); pursue an acquisition to gain pricing power in a competitive market. Cost side: upgrade fleet to more fuel-efficient or longer-lived vehicles (subject to cost-benefit analysis); capture operational synergies through M&A (equipment, repairs, shared services); review and reduce overhead costs such as marketing and labor.

questions.prompt: Question 3: How would you value the company? Walk through the P&L and then the valuation method.
questions.guidance: Start with Revenue (ticket price × capacity × number of trips). Subtract gross costs (fixed and variable) to reach EBITDA. Note that comparable transaction multiples could be applied to EBITDA if recent bus-company deal data exists, but this is uncommon. Proceed to FCF: subtract D&A from EBITDA to get EBIT; apply tax rate to get Net Income. FCF = Net Income − change in Net Fixed Assets (Capex minus D&A) − change in Net Working Capital (current assets like cash/AR/inventory minus automatic sources like AP and accruals). Discount FCF at appropriate WACC to arrive at enterprise value.

steps: 16 departures × 2 cities = 32 one-way trips per day
Annual revenue = $19,200 × 365 ≈ $7.0M (rough order of magnitude only)
Subtract fixed costs (bus ownership/leasing, terminal, labor) and variable costs (fuel, maintenance) to reach EBITDA
EBITDA − D&A = EBIT; EBIT × (1 − tax rate) = Net Income
Apply DCF at WACC or EV/EBITDA multiple
math.answer: Enterprise value derived from discounted FCF; comparable multiples as a cross-check if transaction data available

brainstorming.prompt: What are all the ways this bus company could increase its profits?

categories.name: Revenue — Ancillary Services
ideas: Sell snacks and beverages on buses
Sell magazines and newspapers on buses or in terminal
Partner with retail or food vendors in terminal

categories.name: Revenue — Schedule Expansion
ideas: Add more departures (earlier or later runs where demand exists)
Add express or premium service tier at higher price point

categories.name: Revenue — M&A / Pricing Power
ideas: Acquire a competitor to reduce competition and gain pricing power
Joint venture or partnership to expand route network

categories.name: Cost — Fleet Efficiency
ideas: Use buses with longer useful life to reduce replacement frequency
Reduce maintenance costs through better fleet management

categories.name: Cost — Operational Synergies
ideas: Post-acquisition synergies on equipment and repairs
Bulk purchasing for fuel and supplies

categories.name: Cost — Overhead Reduction
ideas: Reduce marketing spend through better targeting

recommendation: In the short term, focus on ancillary revenue streams (on-bus and terminal retail) since the company is already at capacity and cannot raise ticket prices in this competitive market
In the medium term, evaluate a fleet upgrade to reduce operating costs and conduct M&A analysis to gain pricing power
risks: Ancillary revenue initiatives require capital investment and may disrupt customer experience if poorly executed
Acquisition could increase leverage and integration risk; pricing power gains are not guaranteed
Fleet upgrade has significant upfront capex with uncertain payback period
next_steps: Quantify potential ancillary revenue uplift vs. implementation cost
Identify potential acquisition targets and run preliminary valuation
Commission fleet efficiency analysis comparing current vs. upgraded bus economics
